If an auto‑debit fails, the fund house does not charge a penalty, but your bank may levy a fee for the failed debit. The exact amount depends on your bank.
In this demo you can pause a SIP for 1 to 3 months. After the pause period the SIP restarts automatically at the same amount.
Yes, after you pause the SIP it will automatically restart on its own after the pause period ends.
You can lower the SIP amount as long as it stays above the fund's minimum, which in this demo is ₹100.
Yes, after cancelling a SIP you can start a new one later, which may require a new mandate. Your previously invested units stay invested and continue moving with the market.
Stopping a SIP does not trigger any tax; tax applies only when you redeem (sell) units.
Pausing a SIP does not attract any exit load; exit load applies only when you redeem units.

Cancelling the mandate at your bank means the automatic debits will fail, so the next instalment will not be taken. The SIP itself remains active, but you may see a failed payment and possibly a bank fee. To keep the SIP running, update the mandate in the app or set a new one.

If you pause today, the request may take a few working days, so the instalment scheduled for tomorrow could still be processed. The SIP will resume after the pause period once the request is completed.

Yes, lowering the amount keeps the SIP active as long as the new amount is above the minimum (₹100 in this demo). The SIP continues with the reduced instalment while the units already bought stay invested.

Pausing stops the SIP instalments for a set period (1 to 3 months) and then it restarts automatically at the same amount, so the future contributions are delayed (R3). Lowering reduces the monthly amount to a smaller value, such as ₹200, while keeping the SIP active each month, so you continue contributing but with less money (R4).
